activities.anchor: behave the same wherever they appear
activities.caption: pair each group with its personality
activities.name: ogGroupMatch

config.prompt: Four groups, four personalities — pair each with its signature consequence:

pairs.right: hydrogen bonding — ethanol boils at 78 °C where ethane boils at −89 °C
donates H⁺ — vinegar, citrus, every fatty acid's head
the bond joining amino acids — the same one Kevlar uses to stop bullets
reactive handle where new bonds form — vanilla, formaldehyde, most drug synthesis

config.why: The group's own electrons, not the carbon skeleton, dominate its local chemistry — learn the twenty or so groups and you can predict behaviour across the whole subject.

activities.anchor: counting from the end that gives the lowest locants
activities.caption: fill the blanks — names are executable code
activities.name: ogNameCloze

config.text: The stem counts carbons (meth-, eth-, prop-, %%0%%-), the suffix names the family (-ane alkane, -ol alcohol, -oic acid carboxylic acid), and numbers locate branches — counting from the end that gives the %%1%% locants. So CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₃ is %%2%%.
config.hint: Four carbons give the fourth stem; the numbering rule minimises the position numbers.

activities.name: ccAdditionBuckets

config.prompt: The C=C bond's three favourite reagents. File each outcome:

items.label: decolourising orange bromine water — the alkene test

activities.anchor: The industrial route to ethanol skips the ladder entirely
activities.caption: drag the divider — two ways to one molecule
activities.name: ogEthanolCompare

config.prompt: Industrial vs biological ethanol — drag the divider:

before.label: industrial
before.text: Ethene + steam over phosphoric acid at 300 °C and 60 atm — the hydration reaction. Cheap, fast, and fed by cracking.

after.label: biological
after.text: Yeast ferments glucose — C₆H₁₂O₆ → 2C₂H₅OH + 2CO₂ — with enzymes, slower but renewable. The same reaction that makes bread rise and beer beer.

config.why: Ethanol is the meeting point of the two chemistries: one molecule, two civilisations' worth of manufacturing.

activities.caption: call the pH — the polite acid
activities.name: ogVinegarEstimate

config.prompt: Ethanoic acid has Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵. A 0.1 mol/L solution sits at roughly what pH?
config.why: About 2.9 — a genuine acid, but with barely 1 per cent of its molecules ionised against hydrochloric acid's essentially complete ionisation at the same concentration.
config.context: That resonance-moderated strength is why you can put vinegar on chips.

activities.anchor: two different functional groups meet, join, and kick out a small molecule
activities.caption: one line of the condensation summary is wrong
activities.name: ogCondensationSpot

config.prompt: One line of this condensation-polymer summary is wrong. Find it.
lines: Addition polymerisation stitches monomers with π electrons — all-or-nothing chains
Condensation joins two different functional groups and kicks out a small molecule, usually water
Dicarboxylic acid + diol → polyester (PET); dicarboxylic acid + diamine → polyamide (nylon, Kevlar, proteins)
Condensation polymers need monofunctional monomers so the chains stay short and controllable
The by-product must be removed or the equilibrium stops — hence nylon factories pulling water out of the melt
config.correction: Monomers must be at least bifunctional, or the chain cannot continue.
config.why: Condensation lets you tune chain length with reagent ratios — the price of that control is by-product removal.

activities.anchor: comes in two non-superimposable mirror images
activities.caption: true or false — chemistry's handedness
activities.name: ogChiralJudge

statements.s: A carbon carrying four different groups exists as two mirror-image forms — enantiomers, like left and right hands.
statements.why: The two forms are non-superimposable: handedness built from 3-D geometry, not a single carbon's label.

statements.s: The two forms rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions.
statements.why: The historic way they were told apart.

statements.s: Enantiomers behave identically toward enzymes and receptors.
statements.why: Enzymes and receptors are themselves single-handed, so they taste the difference — one carvone smells of caraway, the other of spearmint.

statements.s: The thalidomide tragedy is why every new drug today is synthesised and tested chirality by chirality.
statements.why: One hand eased morning sickness; the other caused severe birth defects — and the drug was sold as a mixture.
